solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Blemishes on the outside of holy books church found in random inspections

indicators.note: the blemishes word is placed around the books and church, so it sits on their outside

parts.note: specks are small marks or blemishes
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of holy books

explanation.surface: Someone finds marks on the covers of the church's Bibles during unannounced checks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blemishes' looks like a plain description, but its word is split open to hold the other two pieces; 'found in' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unannounced or random examinations are what checks made on the spot are called.

clue.text: Supporting singer-songwriter for the public good

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
Bono is the lead singer and songwriter of the Irish band U2

explanation.surface: A star musician backs a charitable cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Bono, famous for charity campaigning, makes the surface especially apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes work, typically legal, done without charge in the public interest.

clue.text: Book that's beginning with account of someone's life

indicators.note: the beginning of the word that's is its opening letter

parts.note: an obit, short for obituary, is a published account of a dead person's life

explanation.surface: A book that opens with a biography of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha, included in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocryphal scripture named after its pious hero is one of the books of the Bible in some canons.

clue.text: Old fashioned wedding's exciting he-men? Nay!

definitions.note: an archaic adjective meaning of or relating to a wedding; the possessive matches its adjectival role

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters of these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A bride turns down the macho men who were supposed to make the old-style wedding thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Hymen, the Greek god of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adjective describes anything belonging to marriage, from Hymen, the classical god of weddings.

clue.text: Number participating in nasty cults, 19 resulting in pride, murder etc

indicators.note: the number word joins in with the cults and the answer at 19, and nasty says the whole lot is messed up and rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer at 19 across, which is VIOLENCE

explanation.surface: Members of violent cults end up committing crimes such as murder.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters keep NO together in the middle, so it can also be read as NO going inside a rearrangement. Pride (of lions) and murder (of crows) are group names, though they read like sins.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride of lions and a murder of crows are examples of words naming groups of animals.

clue.text: Party thus faces anger, end of tolerance

indicators.note: the word for thus comes first, facing what follows it

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
ire is a literary word for anger

indicators.note: the end of tolerance is its final letter

explanation.surface: A party loses its patience as its anger runs out of tolerance.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening social gathering, often a fairly elegant one, is a kind of party.

clue.text: Front of pole lost in river

indicators.note: points at the first letter of the pole word as the one to go
lost means that front letter is taken away

parts.note: a staff is a pole or stick

explanation.surface: Someone loses the front of a pole in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh waterway runs from the Brecon Beacons to the sea at Cardiff.

clue.text: Line up for daring challenge

parts.note: a high wire stretched up in the air for a performer to walk along, a daring feat

explanation.surface: People queue to take on a dare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line up' reads as queueing, but it is a rope strung up high for a daredevil to cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut cord raised high for acrobats is literally a line up there for a daring act.

clue.text: Decorative piece on garment creating storm

definitions.meaning: a wide ornamental frill or ruffle sewn on a skirt or dress
to storm off is to move away angrily and dramatically

explanation.surface: A dress trimming causes a furious row.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a gathered ornamental strip on clothing and to flounder off in a temper.

clue.text: Brothers returning for service

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for brothers is read backwards

explanation.surface: Brothers come back to attend a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is the service tree, a kind of rowan, not a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The service tree is a European tree also called by this short botanical name.

clue.text: Gent involved with plot, I'm in a situation of change and uncertainty

definitions.text: a situation of change and uncertainty
definitions.note: a place or state where different elements are mixing and nothing is settled

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters of these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gentleman caught up in a plot finds himself in an uncertain position.
explanation.definitionFit: The figurative sense is a fluid place where ingredients or cultures blend and nothing is fixed yet.

clue.text: US city street in favour

indicators.note: the street abbreviation is placed inside the word for favour

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing

explanation.surface: An American city where one street is popular.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Massachusetts is a major city in the United States.

clue.text: Regular obsession, not hard when it comes to sport

parts.note: even means regular, steady

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is dropped from the obsession word

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed by it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone's constant fixation softens when sport is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Eventing is an equestrian competition combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-phase horse-riding competition is an Olympic sport.

clue.text: Type of sound made by boy shouting about love

indicators.note: the boy and the shouting together go around the letter for love

parts.note: a son is a boy
a rant is loud angry shouting
O stands for love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A noise made by a lad yelling about love.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics this is a speech sound made with free airflow, such as a vowel, nasal or liquid.

clue.text: I'd obey all that's ordered in court

indicators.note: ordered means arranged in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A defendant promises to do whatever the court orders.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the popular name of the Central Criminal Court in London.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Central Criminal Court is widely known by this name for its street.

clue.text: Poet seen as old and modern, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means the word for modern is read backwards

parts.note: new means modern

explanation.surface: A poet regarded as both traditional and modern, viewed in hindsight.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Owen was the English poet of the First World War known for Dulce et Decorum Est.

clue.text: Bargain that you would expect from reliable timber merchant?

definitions.text: Bargain that you would expect from reliable timber merchant?

parts.words: Bargain that you would expect from reliable timber merchant?
parts.note: a bargain, and also the quality pine or fir a trustworthy wood dealer would sell

explanation.surface: A dependable wood supplier should offer good value.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a trade name for fir or pine timber, so a reliable timber seller literally supplies it in good quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an advantageous purchase, and punningly also high-quality fir planks.

clue.text: Raised money, disposing of article

indicators.note: disposing of means the article is got rid of from the money word

parts.note: bread is slang for money
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Funds were raised by getting rid of an item.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised as in reared or brought up, as children or livestock are.

clue.text: Fruit tree growing up on trellis, one not showing deterioration

indicators.note: in a down clue, growing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards
not showing means the letter for one is hidden away, removed

parts.note: an espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a trellis or wall, as 'on trellis' says
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fruit tree climbing a trellis shows no sign of decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on trellis' describes the espalier; removing I gives ESPALER, which 'growing up' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling back into illness or bad habits after improvement is a form of deterioration.

clue.text: Old man into wickedness and aggression

indicators.note: the old-man letters go into the word for wickedness

parts.note: vice is wickedness
Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: An elderly man is drawn into wickedness and hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical force meant to hurt is aggressive behaviour, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Standard work in the third tier of the first form?

definitions.meaning: a book or piece regarded as a model of its kind

definitions.text: in the third tier of the first form?
definitions.meaning: a pupil in Class 1C, the C stream of the first-year form, which reads as letters CLASS, 1 and C

explanation.surface: A set text studied by a junior school class.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools often split a year (form) into streams A, B, C, so the third stream of form 1 is class 1C; read 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of lasting excellence that sets the standard for others is a classic one.

clue.text: Grub is awful in coastal region

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The food served on a stretch of coast is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Sur is a rugged stretch of the central California coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This rugged Californian shoreline area between Carmel and San Simeon is a coastal region.

clue.text: Dog squatted, one occupying a ground taken short

indicators.note: the squatting and one letters occupy a space inside the other part
taken short means the ground word loses its last letter

parts.note: land is ground
sat means squatted down
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dog squats on a patch of ground, caught short.
explanation.walkthrough: SATI goes inside A + LAN, LAND shortened by 'taken short'; 'taken short' also hints at a dog needing a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The German shepherd breed is known in Britain by this name.

clue.text: Cathedral dignitary, this person being held in dishonour

indicators.note: the speaker is held inside the dignitary's title

parts.note: a dean is the head of a cathedral chapter
the setter refers to themself as this person, giving ME

explanation.surface: A cathedral official has the speaker held in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase or lower someone in dignity is to bring disgrace upon them.

clue.text: Olympic athlete to contend for victory in film

parts.note: Mo Farah is a British Olympic distance-running champion
to vie is to compete for a win

explanation.surface: An Olympian competes to win in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema picture is commonly called a film or a flick.

clue.text: Squishy food device hairy man provided for Scot

indicators.note: the hairy man is provided in place of the Scot, standing in for him

parts.note: an appliance is a device
Ian is a typically Scottish name
in Genesis, Esau is described as a hairy man

explanation.surface: A gadget for making mushy food that a hairy man supplied to a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided for' means 'substituted for': IAN in APPLIANCE is swapped for ESAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed, puréed fruit is soft and mushy, served with pork.

clue.text: Container with lubricant, not commercial product

indicators.note: not means the product word is taken away from the lubricant

parts.note: Vaseline is a brand of petroleum jelly used as a lubricant
a line is a range or type of goods sold

explanation.surface: A container holding lubricant that is not on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental vessel for flowers is a kind of container.

clue.text: Very hard stuff putting maiden off — that's strange

indicators.note: with off, putting off means sending the maiden letter away
completes the instruction to remove the maiden from the hard stuff

parts.note: emery is a very hard rock used as an abrasive
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Hard stuff puts a young woman off, which seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: EERY is a variant spelling of eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and unsettling, uncanny things can be called strange.

clue.text: Soldiers quiet, crossing island in spring

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers

indicators.note: the word for quiet crosses over, going around, the island letter

parts.note: silence is quiet

explanation.surface: Troops keep silent while crossing an island in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Springiness or elasticity, the ability to bounce back, is this quality.
